Subject: Post-call: Novus Clinical model-fit & Redwood eval next steps

Hi Aisha — great to meet you and Mark on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

1) Use case summary (as we heard it)
- Primary: patient note summarization + downstream triage flagging (high/medium/low).
- Secondary: extract structured problem lists from free-text notes for analytics.
- Volume: ~3M notes/year, spike patterns during intake windows.

2) Immediate objectives from Novus Clinical
- Run a small, customer-specific eval to validate: (a) summary fidelity, (b) triage classification accuracy, (c) entity extraction precision/recall.
- Understand latency/throughput requirements for near-real-time triage (target P95 < 250ms on dedicated capacity for short notes).

3) Redwood recommendation (initial)
- Model family: start with a comparsion set: redwood-instruct-med-13b (fp16) and a quantized Llama-2-13b-chat variant (q4*).
- Reasoning: 13B variants balance quality/cost for your expected throughput; we can pivot to 70B variants if summaries underperform.

4) Eval plan (what we need from you)
- Small sample CSV (attached: baseline_sample.csv) with columns: id, note_text, gold_summary, gold_triage_label, metadata(patient_age, department). Please send ~500 examples for an initial run.
- Privacy: if notes are PHI, please provide a de-identified export or confirm transfer via your secure S3 (we support direct S3/GCS uploads into a private Redwood eval workspace).

5) Next steps / timeline
- You: share sample data + brief on any redlines (compliance/contract) by Thu 03/31.
- Redwood: we run an initial eval within 3 business days of receiving sample and share results + scoring notebook.
- Follow-up: 30-minute walkthrough to review metrics and decide model + quantization plan.

Attached: baseline_sample.csv (sample format), redwood_eval_template.xlsx (scoring template), novus-demo-notes.pdf (call notes).

If this matches your expectation, I’ll have Priyom scope the eval run and send the secure upload instructions. Thanks — excited to get this moving.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0187

Subject: RE: Post-call: Novus Clinical model-fit & Redwood eval next steps — eval setup & scoring details

Hi Aisha — following Grace's recap, I’m looping in the eval-run specifics so you have a self-contained checklist. We can also run this together over a call if you prefer.

1) De-id & transfer options- Template: we recommend removing name/SSNs/IDs and keeping clinical timestamps & note structure. If you want, use our de-id checklist: remove direct PII, keep symptom phrases, hash any IDs. If you can’t de-id, we accept uploads into a private S3 bucket with a short-term role we provide (we’ll send a presigned + role).

2) Dataset format (required)- Format: CSV or newline-delimited JSON (ndjson).
- Required columns/fields: id, note_text, gold_summary, gold_triage_label, patient_age, department, source_file, created_at.
- Example row (CSV):
  id_001,"Pt presents with chest pain...","Patient reported chest pain; no acute ischemia suspected; recommend cardiology follow-up.",urgent,62,ED,note_20270103_45,2027-01-03T09:14:00Z

3) Eval metrics & scoring criteria- Summary quality: ROUGE-L and human-judged fidelity (1-5) on 200 sampled notes; target ROUGE-L >= 0.45 to pass initial bar.
- Triage classification: macro F1 >= 0.78 preferred; also report per-class precision/recall (urgent must have recall >= 0.92).
- Extraction (entities/problem-list): micro F1 >= 0.80.
- Latency: P95 token-latency target < 250ms for short notes on dedicated 1-GPU config (we’ll profile post-eval).

4) Models & run configuration- Baseline set to run (initial eval):
  * redwood-instruct-med-13b-fp16 (quality baseline)
  * llama2-chat-13b-q4 (cost-optimized candidate)
  * redwood-mini-7b-q4 (fast baseline to show scaling)
- We’ll run deterministic scoring and also a stochastic pass for 100 titles to evaluate variance. We recommend config: max_new_tokens=512, temperature=0.0 (for classification/extraction), temperature=0.2 for generation sampling pass.

5) Guardrails & regression monitoring- We’ll add a baseline snapshot to Redwood Optimize so future model upgrades trigger a regression alert if ROUGE or F1 drops > 5 percentage points.

6) Deliverables & timeline- After you upload: initial run 48–72 hours. Deliverable: results CSV + scoring notebook + short summary deck.

7) Operational notes- Upload options: (A) Grant Redwood an STS role to your S3 path, (B) presigned upload to our eval workspace, (C) upload to shared Drive (encrypted link).
- Permissions: please include an engineer contact who can attach an STS role if you choose option A.

If this looks good, Grace will create the eval job and send secure upload instructions. Ben — can you please add the HubSpot deal link and assign the internal owner for the run?

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
